title: Live-Db2 integration coverage — every feature beyond STEP-7's baseline, verified against a real database, not mocks
description: STEP-7 built the integration-test harness itself (tests/integration/, gated behind the `integration` pytest marker, auto-skipped unless DB2_DATABASE is set, wired into CI by PH-2 as the `integration-test` job running `pytest -m integration -v --no-cov`) and used it to cover only the STEP-1..7 baseline: CRUD round-trips, vector-search nearest-neighbour correctness, scope isolation, TTL purge, forget/tombstone, optimistic concurrency, and the three original adapters (LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP). Every feature shipped since — all four of EPIC-2 (ENH-1..4), all four of EPIC-3 (ORC-1..4), all six of EPIC-7 (PIPE-1..6), and all ten of EPIC-8 (THRD-1..10) — was verified in its own story only with unit tests against a mocked/fake ibm_db_dbi cursor (confirmed by grepping tests/integration/*.py: none of get_context_card, content_hash, min_confidence, reconcile, consolidated_at, hybrid, chunk, SchemaPolicy, IngestResolver, erase_all, export_scope/import_scope, add_messages/get_messages/delete_message, add_memory/add_user/add_agent, get_summary, MemoryExtractor, the Thread class, delete_user/delete_agent, delete_memory, the *_async methods, or exact_agent_match/exact_thread_match appear anywhere in the integration suite). A mocked cursor cannot catch what only a real Db2 engine can: actual VECTOR_DISTANCE/TO_VECTOR/VECTOR_SERIALIZE SQL correctness, real row-level locking behavior under concurrent claim races (ENH-4's _claim_consolidated), real JSON-column metadata-filter predicates, real SQLCODE errors, or an actual cross-scope data leak in the VER-5-audited isolation core (THRD-10's exact_agent_match=False fuzzy mode). This epic closes that gap: every story below adds one new file under tests/integration/, written against a live Db2 instance using the existing tests/integration/conftest.py fixtures (db2_pool / migrated_pool / store / unique_agent_id / scope / thread_scope / vec_dim / zero_vec / make_unit_vec) and the same class-per-behavior style as test_core.py, requires zero CI changes (PH-2's `pytest -m integration` already collects any new file under tests/integration/ automatically), and — following STEP-7's own precedent of the base.py docstring fix it found along the way — fixes any genuine bug a live run surfaces (not a test-authoring mistake) and records it in DECISIONS.md, rather than only asserting coverage. Designed for maximum parallelism: LIVE-1 through LIVE-18 are fully independent — each authors exactly one new test file, reads existing source only, and edits no file any other LIVE-* story edits (define fixtures locally inside your own file rather than editing the shared conftest.py, to keep every story mergeable in any order) — safe to run as eighteen simultaneous subagents. LIVE-19 (the coverage audit) depends on all eighteen and must run last. THRD-10's live scope-matching story (LIVE-18) carries the same high-blast-radius warning EPIC-8 itself flagged: it must only add read-only, real-data leak-detection assertions, never touch _scope_predicates()/MemoryScope in models.py or repositories/base.py.
